body.heading: Why mornings outside feel different
paragraphs: Daylight, even on a cloudy day, is far brighter than indoor lighting. Getting some of it, especially earlier in the day, is a cue many people's bodies use to feel awake in the day and sleepier at night.
This is general information, not medical advice, and it needs no special equipment: a walk to the corner, tea on a doorstep, or a seat by a bright window all count for something.

body.heading: Build a daylight moment
paragraphs: Pick a moment that already exists and move it outside or nearer the light: the morning drink, the school run, the first phone call of the day. Ten minutes is a fine start.
While you are out there, use the minutes well. Look at the sky, notice the season, watch the street do its morning things. Daylight plus attention is a small daily holiday.

takeaway: Move one daily moment toward the daylight and enjoy being in it.
